## Description {#details}



<p>Every session is obtained through onboarding. The canonical app startup is: try qar_runtime_rejoin with the persisted <a href="/api/qar-streaming-c/structs/qaronboardingid">QarOnboardingId</a>; when that fails, show the onboarding GUI and run qar_runtime_onboard. Persist the id the onboard call returns — it is the ticket for every later rejoin / forget. Destroy the session handle to tear the session down while keeping persisted state; use qar_runtime_forget for a full reset.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Run full onboarding using exactly one chained mode extension.</p>


<p>Chain one of:</p>


<ul class="doxyList ">
<li><a href="/api/qar-streaming-c/structs/qaronboardcodeext">QarOnboardCodeExt</a>: PAKE code shown on the hub onboarding screen</li>
<li><a href="/api/qar-streaming-c/structs/qaronboardinviteext">QarOnboardInviteExt</a>: full invite blob from a sibling instance</li>
</ul>

<p><a href="/api/qar-streaming-c/structs/qaronboardhostext">QarOnboardHostExt</a> is optional and only applies when <a href="/api/qar-streaming-c/structs/qaronboardcodeext">QarOnboardCodeExt</a> is chained.</p>


<p>Optional, alongside the mode extension:</p>


<ul class="doxyList ">
<li><a href="/api/qar-streaming-c/structs/qaronboardpeeridext">QarOnboardPeerIdExt</a>: join under a caller-chosen peer id instead of a fresh one; the id is persisted with the slot and kept by every later rejoin.</li>
<li><a href="/api/qar-streaming-c/structs/qargraphicsdeviceid">QarGraphicsDeviceId</a>: create the session's GPU devices on this adapter. Without it, the session uses the GPU QAROS selected for an application it launched (carried in the launch invite), else one the library picks. Read the adapter in use with <a href="/api/qar-streaming-c/groups/qar-c-session/#ga31f27a3aa22e5cdacc5a008a4a02a586">qar_session_get_graphics_device_id()</a>.</li>

<p>Restore and validate the last persisted session for init-&gt;onboarding_id. Pops no UI.</p>


<p>Blocks until the restore validated or failed. Progress callbacks fire from an internal thread while the caller is blocked; the last progress callback returns before the call does.</p>


<p>Chain <a href="/api/qar-streaming-c/structs/qargraphicsdeviceid">QarGraphicsDeviceId</a> on init-&gt;header.next to create the session's GPU devices on that adapter. The peer id is the one persisted by the onboard.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Ask the hub this session onboarded through for a new set of one-time onboarding codes, for several devices to onboard at once.</p>


<p>Every call mints codes of its own. Codes other callers hold and the code on the hub's onboarding screen stay valid, and none of the new codes is announced or displayed. Each works once, for init-&gt;lifetime_seconds. Hand a device either the invite itself (qar_onboarding_invite_serialize, then <a href="/api/qar-streaming-c/structs/qaronboardinviteext">QarOnboardInviteExt</a>) or its code text (qar_onboarding_invite_get_code, then <a href="/api/qar-streaming-c/structs/qaronboardcodeext">QarOnboardCodeExt</a>). Blocks until the hub answers.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Onboard from a complete invite (init-&gt;invite) received from a sibling instance.</p>


<p>The method (PAKE or password) is auto-detected from the invite. No discovery, no GUI.</p>

<p>Ask the hub this session onboarded through for a fresh onboarding invite to hand to another instance.</p>


<p>The hub peer is resolved internally from the session — nothing to configure. Serialize the delivered invite with qar_onboarding_invite_serialize and send the bytes to the sibling over IPC / shared memory / a pipe.</p>
